title: Identity Lifecycle Fundamentals
description: A guided Academy pack that teaches the Saviynt identity lifecycle from HR import through correlation, lifecycle processing, role evaluation, provisioning, aggregation, and access review readiness.
learningObjectives: Understand the major stages of the identity lifecycle.
Recognize how HR import, correlation, lifecycle policies, roles, provisioning, and aggregation fit together.
Identify where a lifecycle process most likely failed based on observed symptoms.
Distinguish between data import issues, role evaluation issues, provisioning issues, and reconciliation issues.

questions.prompt: Match each identity lifecycle component with its primary responsibility.
rightItems: Brings identity data from an authoritative source into Saviynt
Links imported accounts to the correct identity
Determines what should happen when identity attributes change
Creates, updates, or disables accounts on target systems
Confirms what access actually exists on target systems

correctAnswer.User Import: Brings identity data from an authoritative source into Saviynt
correctAnswer.Account Correlation: Links imported accounts to the correct identity
correctAnswer.Identity Lifecycle Policy: Determines what should happen when identity attributes change
correctAnswer.Provisioning: Creates, updates, or disables accounts on target systems
correctAnswer.Aggregation / Reconciliation: Confirms what access actually exists on target systems

questions.hint: Think about the lifecycle as a pipeline: import the person, link accounts, decide what should happen, perform the action, then verify the result.
questions.explanation: User Import brings people and their attributes into Saviynt. Correlation links accounts to the right identities. Lifecycle policies decide what actions should occur when attributes such as status, department, or job code change. Provisioning performs changes on connected applications, while aggregation verifies the real state of accounts and access on those applications.

questions.prompt: Arrange these steps in the typical order for automated new-hire onboarding.
items: Aggregate endpoint accounts to confirm target-state access
correctAnswer: Aggregate endpoint accounts to confirm target-state access
questions.hint: Saviynt needs identity data before it can evaluate roles or provision access.
questions.explanation: The lifecycle starts with importing the HR record. Saviynt then correlates identity and account data so it understands who the user is. Role logic determines what access the user should receive, provisioning applies that access to target systems, and aggregation later confirms whether the endpoint state matches expectations.

questions.prompt: A Workday User Import job runs during onboarding. Which outcomes are normally expected from this stage? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Create or update the user's identity attributes in Saviynt
Populate values such as department, manager, location, job code, or status
Provide data used later by lifecycle policies and role rules
Automatically guarantee that every endpoint account was created successfully
correctAnswer: Create or update the user's identity attributes in Saviynt
Populate values such as department, manager, location, job code, or status
Provide data used later by lifecycle policies and role rules
questions.hint: User Import is about identity data. It does not prove that downstream provisioning or certification has happened.
questions.explanation: User Import creates or updates identity records and attributes in Saviynt. Those attributes are then used by lifecycle policies, role rules, approval logic, and provisioning decisions. Certification and endpoint account creation are separate downstream processes.

questions.prompt: What does account correlation help prevent or resolve? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Duplicate identities for the same person
Endpoint accounts being linked to the wrong user
HTTP authentication failures during REST provisioning
correctAnswer: Duplicate identities for the same person
Endpoint accounts being linked to the wrong user
questions.hint: Correlation is about identity matching, not connector authentication or campaign scheduling.
questions.explanation: Correlation determines whether imported accounts belong to an existing identity or should be associated differently. Good correlation prevents duplicate identities, incorrect account ownership, and missing identity-account links. REST authentication failures and stale certification data belong to other lifecycle areas.

questions.prompt: A new employee appears in Saviynt after HR import, but their Department field is blank. The employee never receives department-based birthright access. Which area should be investigated FIRST?
questions.correctAnswer: User Import attribute mapping
questions.hint: The role rule may be fine, but it cannot evaluate a department value that never arrived.
questions.explanation: The first visible problem is that the Department attribute is blank in Saviynt. Department-based birthright access depends on that value being imported correctly. Provisioning, certification, and connector authentication occur later and cannot explain why the identity attribute is missing.

questions.prompt: A new employee has the correct Department, Manager, and Location values in Saviynt. A Dynamic Role should assign standard access for that department, but the role is never assigned. Which component is the MOST likely issue?
questions.correctAnswer: Dynamic Role rule configuration
questions.hint: The identity data is already correct, so look at the logic that evaluates that data.
questions.explanation: Because the identity attributes are present and correct, User Import is probably working. The next likely failure point is the Dynamic Role rule itself, such as the wrong attribute, unexpected value format, inactive role, or incorrect condition. Access reviews and aggregation do not assign the role.

questions.prompt: Match each symptom with the lifecycle stage most likely responsible.
leftItems: Employee exists in HR but not in Saviynt
Employee has correct attributes but no birthright access
Provisioning task exists but endpoint account is not created
Account exists on endpoint but does not appear in Saviynt
questions.hint: Identify the earliest point in the lifecycle where the observed symptom could have been introduced.
questions.explanation: Missing identities point to import. Duplicate identities point to correlation. Correct identity data with missing role-based access points to role evaluation. Created tasks with no endpoint result point to provisioning. Endpoint access missing from Saviynt points to aggregation or reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Arrange the typical termination lifecycle in the correct order.
items: HR system marks the employee as terminated
User Import updates the identity status in Saviynt
Lifecycle policy evaluates the termination event
Aggregation confirms the account state on target systems
correctAnswer: HR system marks the employee as terminated
User Import updates the identity status in Saviynt
Lifecycle policy evaluates the termination event
Aggregation confirms the account state on target systems
questions.hint: The termination begins in the authoritative source, then Saviynt reacts to the updated identity state.
questions.explanation: The HR source records the termination first. Saviynt imports that status, lifecycle logic determines the required response, provisioning disables or removes access, and aggregation confirms whether the target systems reflect the expected terminated state.

questions.prompt: A terminated employee still appears to have active access in Saviynt. Which areas should be checked before assuming provisioning failed? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Whether the HR termination status was imported into Saviynt
Whether the lifecycle policy executed for the termination event
Whether the user's preferred language was configured
Whether the certification campaign was given a custom name
correctAnswer: Whether the HR termination status was imported into Saviynt
Whether the lifecycle policy executed for the termination event
questions.hint: Work backward from the symptom. Confirm the trigger, the lifecycle decision, and task creation before blaming the connector.
questions.explanation: A termination failure can occur at multiple stages. The HR status may not have imported, the lifecycle policy may not have triggered, or deprovisioning tasks may not have been created. User language and campaign naming are not meaningful causes of active access after termination.

questions.prompt: An employee transfers from Sales to Finance. The HR import succeeds and the user's Department changes to Finance in Saviynt. The Finance role is assigned, but the old Sales access remains after provisioning completes. Which configuration should be investigated FIRST?
choices: Lifecycle or role removal logic for department changes
questions.correctAnswer: Lifecycle or role removal logic for department changes
questions.hint: The new access was assigned successfully. Focus on why old access was not removed.
questions.explanation: The import and new role assignment worked, so the issue is not the HR feed or Finance role assignment. The remaining problem is access cleanup during a department change. Lifecycle policy logic, role removal behavior, or deprovisioning configuration should be reviewed.

questions.prompt: Match each identity lifecycle event with the most appropriate automated response.
rightItems: Create identity and grant baseline access
Reevaluate role assignments and remove access no longer needed
Update approval routing and reporting relationships
Disable or remove accounts and access
Reactivate or reestablish access according to current attributes

correctAnswer.New hire: Create identity and grant baseline access
correctAnswer.Department transfer: Reevaluate role assignments and remove access no longer needed
correctAnswer.Manager change: Update approval routing and reporting relationships
correctAnswer.Termination: Disable or remove accounts and access
correctAnswer.Rehire: Reactivate or reestablish access according to current attributes

questions.hint: Think in terms of what changed about the person and what Saviynt should adjust as a result.
questions.explanation: Each lifecycle event should drive a different governance response. New hires need baseline access, transfers require reevaluation, manager changes affect approval and ownership relationships, terminations require deprovisioning, and rehires require careful reactivation based on current identity data.

questions.prompt: A company wants to make onboarding safer before enabling automatic provisioning to production systems. Which validations should be performed? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Confirm required HR attributes are imported and mapped correctly
Test correlation using realistic employee and contractor records
Validate birthright and dynamic role conditions
Confirm provisioning tasks are generated for the correct endpoints
correctAnswer: Confirm required HR attributes are imported and mapped correctly
Test correlation using realistic employee and contractor records
Validate birthright and dynamic role conditions
Confirm provisioning tasks are generated for the correct endpoints
questions.hint: Before production provisioning, validate the data, matching logic, access logic, and task generation.
questions.explanation: Safe onboarding depends on accurate identity data, correct account correlation, correct role evaluation, and proper task generation. Aggregation should not be disabled permanently because it is needed to verify target-state access and detect drift.

questions.prompt: A new hire is imported correctly and receives the expected Business Role. Saviynt creates provisioning tasks for Active Directory, SAP, and Salesforce. Active Directory and SAP accounts are created successfully, but Salesforce is not. Aggregation later confirms no Salesforce account exists. Which component should be investigated FIRST?
questions.correctAnswer: Salesforce endpoint provisioning configuration
questions.hint: The lifecycle reached provisioning, and only one target application failed.
questions.explanation: User Import, correlation, and role evaluation all succeeded because the identity exists, the role was assigned, and provisioning tasks were generated. Since only Salesforce failed while other endpoints succeeded, the issue is most likely isolated to Salesforce provisioning configuration, connector settings, or endpoint-specific mappings.

questions.prompt: Arrange the correct troubleshooting sequence for a user who did not receive expected birthright access.
items: Verify whether provisioning tasks were created
Verify whether the identity exists in Saviynt
Verify whether required identity attributes were imported correctly
Verify whether role or lifecycle rules matched the identity
correctAnswer: Verify whether the identity exists in Saviynt
Verify whether required identity attributes were imported correctly
Verify whether role or lifecycle rules matched the identity
Verify whether provisioning tasks were created
questions.hint: Start at the beginning of the lifecycle instead of jumping directly to the connector.
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting should follow the lifecycle path. First confirm the identity exists, then confirm its attributes are correct. Next check whether lifecycle or role logic matched the identity, then whether provisioning tasks were created, and finally whether endpoint provisioning succeeded.

questions.prompt: A company uses Workday as the authoritative source and provisions access to Active Directory, SAP, and Salesforce. A new Finance employee is imported successfully, the identity has the correct Department and Job Code, correlation links the identity correctly, and the Finance Business Role is assigned. Provisioning tasks are created for all three applications. Active Directory and SAP accounts are created, but Salesforce access is missing. The next aggregation confirms the Salesforce account was never created. Where is the MOST likely failure?
questions.correctAnswer: Salesforce provisioning configuration
questions.hint: Every earlier lifecycle stage succeeded. The failure appears only when provisioning one target application.
questions.explanation: This is a full lifecycle troubleshooting scenario. User Import succeeded because the identity and attributes are correct. Correlation succeeded because the account ownership is linked correctly. Role evaluation succeeded because the Finance Business Role was assigned and tasks were generated. Since only Salesforce failed while Active Directory and SAP succeeded, the most likely issue is Salesforce-specific provisioning configuration, connector setup, or account creation mapping.

lesson.title: Before you begin: the identity lifecycle pipeline
content: In Saviynt, the identity lifecycle starts when trusted identity data is imported from an authoritative source such as Workday or another HR system.
After the identity exists in the Identity Warehouse, Saviynt can correlate accounts, evaluate lifecycle policies, assign birthright or dynamic roles, and generate provisioning tasks.
Provisioning applies the intended changes to connected target systems such as Active Directory, SAP, or Salesforce.
Aggregation and reconciliation confirm what actually exists on the target systems after provisioning, which helps detect drift, stale data, and failed changes.
When troubleshooting lifecycle issues, follow the pipeline in order: identity data, correlation, lifecycle policy, role evaluation, provisioning, then aggregation.
keyTakeaways: Do not blame provisioning until you confirm the identity, attributes, lifecycle logic, and role assignment are correct.
Aggregation verifies target-state access; it does not create the initial lifecycle decision.
A clean lifecycle process depends on accurate identity attributes.

title: Identity Warehouse and Account Correlation
description: A guided Academy pack that teaches how Saviynt represents identities, accounts, attributes, ownership, and correlation between imported accounts and Identity Warehouse users.
learningObjectives: Understand the difference between identities and endpoint accounts.
Recognize why account correlation is critical in identity governance.
Identify common causes of duplicate identities and orphaned accounts.
Troubleshoot account ownership and correlation issues after aggregation.

questions.prompt: Match each Identity Warehouse concept with its primary meaning.
rightItems: A person or worker represented in Saviynt
A login or account that exists on a target application
The process of linking accounts to the correct identity
An account that is not linked to a known identity
The trusted source for user identity data

correctAnswer.Identity: A person or worker represented in Saviynt
correctAnswer.Endpoint Account: A login or account that exists on a target application
correctAnswer.Account Correlation: The process of linking accounts to the correct identity
correctAnswer.Orphan Account: An account that is not linked to a known identity
correctAnswer.Authoritative Source: The trusted source for user identity data

questions.hint: Separate the person from the account. Saviynt governs both, but they are not the same object.
questions.explanation: An identity represents the person, while endpoint accounts represent that person's presence on target systems. Correlation links the two. If an account cannot be linked to an identity, it may appear as orphaned. The authoritative source, such as Workday, usually supplies the trusted identity record.

questions.prompt: Why is account correlation important during aggregation? Select ALL that apply.
choices: It links imported accounts to the correct identity.
It determines the REST API authentication method.
It replaces the need for entitlement aggregation.
correctAnswer: It links imported accounts to the correct identity.
questions.hint: Correlation is about matching ownership, not connector transport or entitlement collection.
questions.explanation: Correlation ensures accounts imported from endpoints are associated with the right identities. This helps prevent duplicates and exposes accounts that do not match a known user. It does not define API authentication and does not replace entitlement aggregation.

questions.prompt: Arrange the typical account aggregation and correlation flow in the correct order.
items: Review unmatched accounts as potential orphan accounts
Use identity attributes as matching criteria
correctAnswer: Use identity attributes as matching criteria
Review unmatched accounts as potential orphan accounts
questions.hint: Saviynt must first import account data before it can compare it against identity data.
questions.explanation: Aggregation brings account data into Saviynt. Correlation then compares account attributes against identity attributes, applies matching rules, links matched accounts to identities, and leaves unmatched accounts for review or remediation.

questions.prompt: A user exists in Workday and has an identity in Saviynt. After Active Directory aggregation, the user's AD account appears as orphaned. Which area should be investigated FIRST?
choices: Account Correlation rule and attribute mappings
questions.correctAnswer: Account Correlation rule and attribute mappings
questions.hint: The identity exists and the account was imported. The missing piece is the link between them.
questions.explanation: An orphan account means Saviynt imported the account but did not link it to an identity. The most likely issue is correlation logic or the attributes used for matching. Certification, password policy, and access approval do not control identity-account linkage.

questions.prompt: Which attributes are commonly useful for account correlation? Select ALL that apply.
questions.hint: Good correlation attributes should be stable, populated, and unique enough to identify the person.
questions.explanation: Employee ID, email address, and username are commonly used because they can be stable and unique depending on the environment. Manager display name is usually not unique enough, and a random session token is not appropriate for persistent identity matching.

questions.prompt: After onboarding Azure AD, duplicate identities begin appearing. The existing correlation rule uses employeeNumber, but Azure AD accounts do not populate that field. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The Azure AD account data does not contain the attribute required by the correlation rule.
The password policy is too strict.
The Access Request portal is disabled.
questions.correctAnswer: The Azure AD account data does not contain the attribute required by the correlation rule.
questions.hint: The rule can only match against data that is actually imported.
questions.explanation: If the correlation rule depends on employeeNumber but Azure AD does not provide it, Saviynt cannot match the account to the existing identity using that rule. This can result in duplicate identities or unmatched accounts. Certification, password policy, and requestability are not the root cause.

questions.prompt: Match each symptom with the most likely correlation-related cause.
leftItems: Many accounts are orphaned after aggregation
Two identities exist for the same employee
Accounts are linked to the wrong employee
Correlation worked for AD but fails for Azure AD
rightItems: Duplicate identity creation due to weak matching
Correlation rule does not distinguish worker type

correctAnswer.Two identities exist for the same employ: Duplicate identity creation due to weak matching
correctAnswer.Contractors match employee identities in: Correlation rule does not distinguish worker type

questions.hint: Look at whether the issue is missing data, duplicate records, wrong ownership, endpoint-specific mapping, or population overlap.
questions.explanation: Correlation issues usually come from missing attributes, weak match logic, non-unique values, endpoint mapping differences, or rules that do not account for different populations such as employees and contractors.

questions.prompt: A correlation rule is being designed for a mixed workforce of employees, contractors, and service accounts. Which validations should be performed before enabling it broadly? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Confirm selected matching attributes are populated for each worker type.
Test whether the attributes are unique enough to avoid false matches.
Validate behavior when an account has no matching identity.
Confirm the rule cannot accidentally link service accounts to human identities.
Disable all access request workflows permanently.
correctAnswer: Confirm selected matching attributes are populated for each worker type.
Test whether the attributes are unique enough to avoid false matches.
Validate behavior when an account has no matching identity.
Confirm the rule cannot accidentally link service accounts to human identities.
questions.hint: A good correlation rule must handle both successful matches and safe failures.
questions.explanation: Correlation design must consider data completeness, uniqueness, unmatched accounts, and special populations like service accounts. Disabling access request workflows is unrelated and would not improve correlation safety.

questions.prompt: Arrange the recommended troubleshooting sequence for duplicate identities created after a new endpoint aggregation.
items: Compare account attributes imported from the new endpoint
Review the current correlation rule criteria
Check whether required matching attributes are blank or transformed differently
Adjust mapping or correlation logic and retest with sample records
correctAnswer: Review the current correlation rule criteria
Compare account attributes imported from the new endpoint
Check whether required matching attributes are blank or transformed differently
Adjust mapping or correlation logic and retest with sample records
questions.hint: Start with evidence, then compare the rule against the actual imported data.
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting should begin with concrete duplicate examples. Then review the rule, compare it with imported endpoint attributes, identify missing or transformed values, and only then change mappings or rule logic.

questions.prompt: An Active Directory account is linked to the wrong identity because the correlation rule uses first name and last name. Two employees have the same name. What is the BEST corrective approach?
choices: Use a more unique and stable identifier such as employee ID or email where appropriate.
Require manager approval for all correlation decisions.
Move Active Directory to a different Security System.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a more unique and stable identifier such as employee ID or email where appropriate.
questions.hint: The problem is not that correlation exists. The problem is that the matching attributes are too weak.
questions.explanation: First and last name are often not unique enough for reliable correlation. A better approach is to use stable and sufficiently unique identifiers, such as employee ID, email, or a carefully designed combination. Disabling aggregation or moving Security Systems does not solve the matching problem.

questions.prompt: Match each account type with the governance concern it most commonly introduces.
rightItems: Should be linked to a person and governed through normal identity lifecycle
Requires stronger ownership, monitoring, and review
May not belong to a human identity but still needs ownership
May be used by multiple people and needs accountability controls
Has no confirmed owner and may represent governance risk

correctAnswer.Human user account: Should be linked to a person and governed through normal identity lifecycle
correctAnswer.Privileged admin account: Requires stronger ownership, monitoring, and review
correctAnswer.Service account: May not belong to a human identity but still needs ownership
correctAnswer.Shared account: May be used by multiple people and needs accountability controls
correctAnswer.Orphan account: Has no confirmed owner and may represent governance risk

questions.hint: Not every account maps cleanly to a single human identity, but every account still needs governance.
questions.explanation: Human accounts usually follow the identity lifecycle. Privileged accounts need stricter controls. Service and shared accounts may not map directly to a person, but they still need accountable ownership. Orphan accounts are risky because ownership is unknown.

questions.prompt: A company wants to reduce orphan accounts after aggregation. Which actions are appropriate? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Ensure authoritative identity data is complete and current.
Create a review process for accounts that cannot be matched automatically.
Ignore orphan accounts if they belong to production systems.
correctAnswer: Ensure authoritative identity data is complete and current.
Create a review process for accounts that cannot be matched automatically.
questions.hint: Some orphan accounts can be fixed automatically, but some require ownership review.
questions.explanation: Reducing orphan accounts requires better match logic, better endpoint mappings, complete identity data, and a process for accounts that cannot be safely correlated. Ignoring orphan accounts is unsafe, especially on production systems.

questions.prompt: A service account is repeatedly being linked to a human identity because its account name contains a user's employee ID. What should be investigated FIRST?
choices: Whether the correlation rule excludes or separately handles service accounts
Whether the user's password is expired
Whether the Access Request portal is enabled
Whether the certification campaign has enough reviewers
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the correlation rule excludes or separately handles service accounts
questions.hint: Service accounts often need different ownership logic than human accounts.
questions.explanation: The account is being incorrectly correlated because the rule treats service account naming data like human identity data. The rule should account for service account patterns, account type, naming conventions, or ownership fields. Passwords, requestability, and reviewer counts are unrelated to the incorrect link.

questions.prompt: Arrange the safest sequence for validating a new correlation rule before production rollout.
items: Run the rule against representative sample data
Identify false positives and false negatives
Review available identity and account attributes
correctAnswer: Review available identity and account attributes
Run the rule against representative sample data
Identify false positives and false negatives
questions.hint: Understand your data before testing logic against it.
questions.explanation: Correlation validation starts by reviewing available data. The rule should then be tested against representative records, evaluated for false matches and missed matches, corrected as needed, and approved only after retesting confirms safe behavior.

questions.prompt: After onboarding a new SaaS application, aggregation succeeds and thousands of accounts are imported. However, 30% of accounts are orphaned, and several others are linked to the wrong users. The current correlation rule matches on email address, but the SaaS application stores email aliases in the login field while Saviynt identities use corporate primary email. What is the MOST likely root cause?
choices: The endpoint account mapping and correlation criteria do not align with authoritative identity attributes.
The SaaS application should be moved to another Security System.
The certification campaign needs to be launched earlier.
The provisioning workflow requires additional manager approval.
questions.correctAnswer: The endpoint account mapping and correlation criteria do not align with authoritative identity attributes.
questions.hint: Aggregation succeeded. The issue is that the imported values do not match the identity values used by the rule.
questions.explanation: The endpoint successfully imported accounts, but the data used for matching does not align with authoritative identity data. Email aliases in the login field will not reliably match corporate primary email. The solution is to review endpoint mappings, transformation logic, and correlation criteria. Security System placement, campaign timing, and approval workflows do not address incorrect account-to-identity matching.

lesson.title: Before you begin: identities, accounts, and correlation
content: The Identity Warehouse represents people, their attributes, their accounts, and their access relationships inside Saviynt.
An identity is the person. An endpoint account is the account that person uses on a target system. These objects must be linked correctly for governance to work.
Account correlation is the process that determines whether an imported account belongs to an existing identity, should remain unmatched, or has been incorrectly mapped.
Poor correlation can create duplicate identities, orphan accounts, or accounts linked to the wrong person.
Good correlation depends on stable, populated, and sufficiently unique attributes such as employee ID, email, or carefully controlled login identifiers.
keyTakeaways: Correlation is about ownership matching, not provisioning transport.
Endpoint account mappings must align with authoritative identity attributes.
Service accounts, shared accounts, and privileged accounts often need special handling.

title: Security Systems, Endpoints, and Connections
description: A guided Academy pack that teaches how Security Systems, Endpoints, and Connections work together in Saviynt, and how to reason through onboarding, requestability, aggregation, and provisioning issues.

lesson.title: Understanding the application model
content: In Saviynt, a Security System acts as a logical governance container. It groups related applications and helps define how access is governed, requested, reviewed, and owned.
An Endpoint represents a specific target application or system, such as Active Directory, SAP, Salesforce, or a custom database application.
A Connection defines the technical communication path between Saviynt and the target system. It controls how Saviynt imports accounts, imports entitlements, and provisions changes.
These objects are related but not interchangeable. A Security System organizes governance. An Endpoint represents the application. A Connection performs technical communication.

When troubleshooting, identify which layer is failing. If the app is missing from request forms, check requestability and Security System configuration. If accounts are not importing, check endpoint aggregation and mappings. If provisioning fails, check the connection and provisioning configuration.

learningObjectives: Distinguish between Security Systems, Endpoints, and Connections.
Understand how requestability differs from aggregation and provisioning.
Identify the most likely configuration layer responsible for common symptoms.
Troubleshoot application onboarding issues using the correct Saviynt object model.

questions.prompt: Match each Saviynt application model object with its primary purpose.
rightItems: Groups related applications and governance settings
Represents a specific target application or system
Defines the technical communication with the target system
Brings target account data into Saviynt
Controls whether and how users can request access

correctAnswer.Security System: Groups related applications and governance settings
correctAnswer.Endpoint: Represents a specific target application or system
correctAnswer.Connection: Defines the technical communication with the target system
correctAnswer.Account Import: Brings target account data into Saviynt
correctAnswer.Access Request configuration: Controls whether and how users can request access

questions.hint: Separate governance organization from technical connectivity.
questions.explanation: The Security System is the governance container, while the Endpoint represents the target application. The Connection handles technical communication. Account Import brings account data into Saviynt, and Access Request configuration determines how users request access.

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly describe Security Systems in Saviynt? Select ALL that apply.
choices: A Security System can group related endpoints under a governance boundary.
A Security System helps organize access request and review behavior.
A Security System directly performs REST or JDBC calls to target systems.
A Security System can affect whether applications appear as requestable.
A Security System replaces the need for endpoint configuration.
correctAnswer: A Security System can group related endpoints under a governance boundary.
A Security System helps organize access request and review behavior.
A Security System can affect whether applications appear as requestable.
questions.hint: Security Systems organize governance; they do not act as technical connectors.
questions.explanation: Security Systems are governance containers. They can group endpoints and influence request and review behavior. They do not directly perform technical connector operations, and they do not replace endpoint or connection configuration.

questions.prompt: Arrange the typical sequence for onboarding a new connected application into Saviynt.
items: Configure account and entitlement import mappings
Create or associate the Security System
Enable requestability if the application should appear in the request catalog
correctAnswer: Create or associate the Security System
Configure account and entitlement import mappings
Enable requestability if the application should appear in the request catalog
questions.hint: Start with the governance container, then the application object, then technical communication and mappings.
questions.explanation: A typical onboarding flow begins by identifying the Security System and Endpoint. The Connection is then configured so Saviynt can communicate with the target. Import mappings are defined, aggregation and provisioning are tested, and requestability is enabled only after the application is ready for user requests.

questions.prompt: A newly onboarded application aggregates accounts successfully, but users cannot find it in the Access Request portal. Which area should be investigated FIRST?
choices: Security System requestability and Access Request configuration
questions.correctAnswer: Security System requestability and Access Request configuration
questions.hint: Aggregation proves account import works. It does not prove the application is requestable.
questions.explanation: If account aggregation succeeds, the endpoint and connection can retrieve data. The issue is likely that the application is not configured as requestable or is not properly exposed through the Security System and Access Request configuration. Correlation, REST authentication, and certification ownership do not directly control whether users can request the application.

questions.prompt: A connection test succeeds, but account aggregation imports zero accounts. Which areas should be reviewed? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Account import query or filter configuration
Whether the target system actually returns accounts for the configured scope
correctAnswer: Account import query or filter configuration
Whether the target system actually returns accounts for the configured scope
questions.hint: A successful connection test only confirms basic communication, not that the import logic is correct.
questions.explanation: A connection test can succeed even when the account import query, filter, or mappings are incorrect. The target system may also return no accounts for the configured scope. Security System display name and certification schedule do not explain why aggregation imports no accounts.

questions.prompt: Match each symptom with the Saviynt layer most likely responsible.
leftItems: Application is missing from the request catalog
Accounts import but required attributes are blank
Provisioning task exists but target account is not created
Application is grouped under the wrong governance area
questions.hint: Map the symptom to the earliest layer that could cause it.
questions.explanation: Request catalog issues usually belong to requestability and Security System settings. Authentication failures point to the Connection. Blank imported attributes point to mappings. Created tasks that do not change the target system point to provisioning. Incorrect governance grouping points to Security System association.

questions.prompt: A user requests access to an application. The request is approved and a provisioning task is created, but the target application is never updated. Account aggregation still works for the same endpoint. Which area should be investigated FIRST?
choices: Provisioning configuration for the endpoint connection
questions.correctAnswer: Provisioning configuration for the endpoint connection
questions.hint: Import and provisioning can use the same endpoint but different operations or mappings.
questions.explanation: Aggregation working proves Saviynt can read from the endpoint, but provisioning requires separate configuration for write operations. Since the request and task were created, the issue is most likely endpoint provisioning configuration, command mapping, API payload, or connector permissions.

questions.prompt: Which items are important to validate before making a newly onboarded endpoint requestable? Select ALL that apply.
choices: Account aggregation imports expected account data.
Entitlement aggregation imports the correct requestable access values.
Provisioning behavior has been tested safely.
Approval workflow and request forms are configured as expected.
All orphan accounts have been ignored.
correctAnswer: Account aggregation imports expected account data.
Entitlement aggregation imports the correct requestable access values.
Provisioning behavior has been tested safely.
Approval workflow and request forms are configured as expected.
questions.hint: Before users can request access, confirm the application imports, displays, approves, and provisions correctly.
questions.explanation: A requestable endpoint should have reliable account and entitlement imports, safe provisioning behavior, and correct request workflows. Orphan accounts should be reviewed or governed, not ignored.

questions.prompt: Arrange the recommended troubleshooting sequence when an application is missing from the request catalog but aggregation works.
items: Verify the endpoint is associated with the expected Security System
Confirm the application or entitlement is configured as requestable
Check whether user eligibility or request filters hide the option
Confirm aggregation imports the relevant entitlement data
Review request form and approval configuration
